thread.title: Diablo Immortal Highlights Activision Blizzard's Nuanced Mobile Strategy - Activision Blizzard, Inc (NASDAQ:ATVI)

author: John Miller
title: Diablo Immortal Highlights Activision Blizzard's Nuanced Mobile Strategy - Activision Blizzard, Inc (NASDAQ:ATVI)
text:
Though the broader technology market suffered during the fourth quarter, Activision Blizzard ( ATVI ) experienced outsized declines on the back of lowered expectations. While the company did provide strong sales and engagement data for its key Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 launch, some industry watchers lowered elevated expectations following the franchise’s latest release in October. Though analysts have maintained revenue expectations for the fourth quarter following the November conference call, marginally weak guidance led to downward earnings estimates. Additionally, press reports following the call highlighted the continuation of the downward trend in monthly active users during the third quarter.
^IXIC data by YCharts
Coincidentally, alongside the conference call the company faced consumer backlash when the Blizzard division announced a mobile game for the Diablo franchise at their annual event. Both Blizzard’s core gamers and new media gaming commentators expressed derision over the inappropriateness of the franchise for mobile devices. This bad press added to pressure on the stock during November. Adding to the October and November pullbacks is recent news the Bungie studio is splitting from company and taking ownership of the Activision division’s Destiny IP.
When Activision holds its 4 th quarter conference call on February 12 th look for further data supporting strong sales and engagement for Black Ops 4 , despite recent industry concerns. Further, the trend toward lower monthly active users likely abated for the fourth quarter with the strong summer/fall release slate that included: Activision’s Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 , Blizzard’s World of Warcraft: Battle of Azeroth and King’s Candy Crush Friends Saga . Though reports of weakening World of Warcraft usage have surfaced, expect a strong step up in MAU from Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 and a trend reversal at King. And while the loss of Destiny will impact future quarters’ revenues, we may receive color that the earnings impact will be minimal in the short term. Following the call, a key remaining concern will center around the new mobile initiatives, such as Diablo Immortal , and their closely adjacent live services.
Source: Q3 2018 Earnings Slides
Activision’s Evolving Mobile Strategy To best understand Activision’s evolving mobile strategy it is necessary to recognize the company has three distinct divisions: Activision, Blizzard and King. Interestingly, they are each well represented by the three new releases mentioned just above. Activision is known for shooters primarily played on consoles, Blizzard for its multiplayer roleplaying and real-time strategy games played on PCs, and King for its more casual, sometimes social games played on mobile devices or the web. In general, mobile gameplay has not been a significant part of the Activision or Blizzard divisions and their more hardcore player base.
However, Activision has shown success with Call of Duty: Zombies for mobile and Hearthstone’s launch on mobile grew its base for Blizzard. But as discussed above, Blizzard faced significant push back following the announcement of Diablo Immortal for mobile. Of key concern to the fanbase is the smaller screen and no mouse and keyboard control that mobile entails. Further, players are concerned the mobile investment will take resources from the development of the next Diablo release for PC. And last, the community is already questioning how the game will be monetized.
When gamers rebuff efforts to expand a franchise’s base or reject its recurring revenue models, they threaten the longevity of the franchise. To weigh these risks, it is necessary to understand Activision’s historic approach to mobile and judge how well management is prepared to address the concerns above. While we will mostly look at Diablo Immortal below, the ideas relate well to other mobile initiatives and live services more broadly.
ZNGA data by YCharts
In an appearance on CNBC’s Squawk Box following 2011’s Black Friday Activision CEO Bobby Kotick answered questions about the company’s holiday sales. He was challenged by host Andrew Sorkin about Activision’s mobile and social strategy. Sorkin noted an iPad in front of Kotick on the table and pressed Kotick about social game maker Zynga ( ZNGA ) and mobile technology. Zynga was going public on December 16 th of that year. The thrust of the questioning pointed to Activision’s apparent lack of a mobile and social strategy. The following is from my 2011 article Activision’s Careful Social Strategy :
“You have an iPad infront of you…What is the ultimate strategy for Activision on this thing?” asked Sorkin. “I stole this from Senator Toomey,” quipped Kotick (Toomey was the previous guest on the show). Everyone laughed until they realized he was not joking. “You’re not kidding,” stated co-host Becky Quick. “It’s not mine,” said Kotick. Incredulous, Sorkin asked, “It is really not yours?” Kotick: “No, it’s not.”
Sorkin handed Kotick the perfect opportunity to educate the viewers of a key nuance of Activision’s strategy. Sorkin tried to highlight the importance of the iPad by pointing out Kotick had one. But just as Kotick had not adopted an iPad, his company was also moving slowly and carefully before expanding into mobile and social formats, such as Facebook.
Kotick also highlighted the fact that console controllers enhance the experience compared to Apple’s ( AAPL ) iPad and other mobile devices. To a large degree this remains true today. However, the accelerometers in mobile devises can be used for targeting and ease twitch gameplay for casual players in certain titles. This feature was enabled for Call of Duty: Zombies for mobile. As way of example, expect new mobile titles to play very similar to Nintendo’s ( OTCPK:NTDOY ) Switch device while in handheld mode, albeit with virtual thumb sticks as opposed to physical. So too expect some games to enable motion controls as we saw with Fortnite for Switch.
Source: Diablo Immortal Website (link below)
When Kotick appeared in on CNBC in 2011, analysts equated “social” with mobile devices and Facebook. Zynga was focused on using Facebook as a platform and Electronic Arts ( EA ) was expanding on Facebook and had recently made a $300 million investment. Interestingly, Activision was already building their own social networks and saw its business as social-based. Call of Duty’s key component is its multiplayer matches and World of Warcraft is a massively multiplayer online world. Importantly, the social interactions in Activision’s games are richer than what occurs in the average mobile game.
During Blizzard’s yearly event, Diablo lead designer Wyatt Cheng announced Diablo Immortal would put game play first and be massively multiplayer. “We are making a full-fledged action-RPG you can play everywhere, with everyone." Cheng said. The game’s website boasts , “massively multiplayer action in your pocket” and “vast social hubs.”
When Activision acquired King in 2016 , they were not just adding a casual mobile game designer. After five years of careful preparation the company was ready to seriously incorporate mobile gameplay into the Activision and Blizzard franchises and capture synergies with King. At the time Kotick stated the following (emphasis added):
We see great opportunities to create new ways for audiences to experience their favorite franchises, from Candy Crush to World of Warcraft to Call of Duty and more, across mobile devices, consoles and personal computers.
Social aspects of Diablo Immortal will also provide Blizzard monetization opportunities. The aforementioned social hubs will likely provide players options to trade or purchase a limited amount of in-game gear. It should be noted past attempts in Diablo to set up trading systems have generally been unsuccessful as they severely affected gameplay incentives. Based on this prior experience, Blizzard now appears prepared to strike a middle ground between no trading and a full-blown auction house.
Most players welcome live services such as downloadable content, cosmetics or even season passes so long as the base game provided substantial high-quality content and no purchasable items enable pay to win mechanics. Players demand regular updates and fresh in-game content for which they are willing to pay. Activision has over $4 billion in net bookings per year from these live services. They currently represent the majority of revenues and continue to capture share. Though not a perfect measure, Activision’s cost per hour of quality entertainment provides gamers a strong value proposition.
Source: Q3 2018 Earnings Slides
Despite Activision’s relatively well received value propositions, hardcore players and new media commentators have set up a negative narrative surrounding Diablo Immortal . By emphasizing reports that key talent has been diverted to mobile initiatives, they are downplaying the role the mobile game will play in the sustainability of the Diablo franchise more generally. This narrative also characterizes the game as a “cash grab” and implies Blizzard’s partner in China, NetEase ( NTES ), is planning to reskin existing assets to create the game and will likely implement pay to win mechanics into gameplay. Inherent in these new media attacks on NetEase is a mischaracterization of their business practices and bias against the Chinese monetization models. NetEase has been a good steward of World of Warcraft and helped sustain the franchise and allow for reinvestment. They also actively participate in Blizzard’s key esports growth pillar; their Shanghai Dragons are one of the twelve founding Overwatch League teams.
Unfortunately, Blizzard’s messaging has played into the subsequent negative press. Company officials did not anticipate pushback during the Q&A following the Diablo Immortal announcement. At one point the onstage designers ask the audience, “do you guys not have phones?” Rather than provide transparency, the designers choose to dismiss legitimate concerns. Blizzard must refocus the narrative around four key areas:
The quality gameplay with strong multiplayer components. A robust value proposition with fair monetization practices. The virtuous cycle that allows reinvestment in the franchise. A sincere apology for an unwarranted attack on its core audience. In November President and COO Coddy Johnson summed up his expectations for Diablo Immortal and noted some fan discontent. His remarks follow:
And last week, Blizzard announced Diablo Immortal, which will bring this [tentpole] franchise to a mobile audience in both the east and the west. While fan reaction was muted to the announcement, players' hands-on experience [with] this content confirmed what we believe, which is that Diablo mobile will be a very well received game when it releases, and players around the world will love it.
Diablo Immortal was built from the ground up for mobile as an authentic Diablo experience that will make the franchise available to hundreds of millions of people around the globe. We're confident when the game launches, it will be a great experience for new players as well as the extremely loyal and vocal Diablo community.
Source: Q3 2018 Earnings Transcript
Takeaways Expect strong fourth quarter results with contributions from Call of Duty and Candy Crush . MAUs will likely reverse trend and could reach 350 million again, though watch for any weakness in World of Warcraft usage. While 2019 revenue forecasts will be revised down with the loss of Destiny , last week’s 10% drop is likely fully pricing in any short-term earnings that will be missed. Longer-term the loss of Destiny remains significant. In light of these factors and despite significant FX headwinds, company guidance for the fourth quarter non-GAAP revenues including deferrals of $3.048 billion is conservative and $1.27 EPS attainable.
ATVI PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts
Activision management has demonstrated they can balance between providing content having a widespread appeal with sustainable economics but also the play mechanics and monetization schemes the demanding hardcore gamers and the influential new gaming media will support. While the current narrative remains negative, if one looks closely at the Diablo Immortal example, the company is poised to strike the aforementioned balance. Because of this, the main risk going forward is of communication, messaging and public relations, not the company’s ability to address legitimate in-game concerns and drive best of breed experiences with strong value propositions. Looking forward we remain cautiously optimistic at the current earnings multiple.
Disclosure: I am/we are long NTES, AAPL. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
